habitatDescription: Forests dominated by oak, maple, and birch trees that lose their leaves seasonally. These areas provide rich food sources like insects, seeds, and berries, supporting many songbirds and woodpeckers.
Evergreen forests of pine, spruce, and fir trees that provide year-round shelter and seeds. Birds such as chickadees and crossbills thrive in these cooler, dense habitats.
Marshes, swamps, and ponds with standing water and dense vegetation. These habitats support wading birds, waterfowl, and species that feed on aquatic insects and fish.
Salt marshes along the Atlantic coast with grasses and tidal channels. These areas attract shorebirds and seabirds that feed on crustaceans and small fish.
Open fields and meadows with grasses and wildflowers. These habitats are ideal for ground-nesting birds and species that hunt insects or small mammals.
Human-developed areas with parks, gardens, and buildings. Many adaptable bird species, such as pigeons, sparrows, and robins, thrive in these environments.
